text.p: Egyptian authorities have released without charge a British-Egyptian man detained in December 1995 on suspicion of organising violence by Islamist militants, sources close to the case said on Sunday.

Akram Abdelaziz Mahmoud al-Sharif, a naturalised Briton who has a British wife and children but still holds Egyptian nationality, spent more than a year in detention, they said. They could not give the exact date of release.

At the time of his detention, the Interior Ministry said in a statement that Sharif was among the leaders of a suicide unit which had planned explosions in Egypt on behalf of the Islamist militant organisation Jihad.
It said senior Jihad member Abdel-Meguid Abdel-Bari, who Egypt says is on the run in Britain, instructed Sharif to set up a Jihad coordination centre in Egypt to plan attacks.

The international Arabic-language newspaper al-Hayat said on Sunday investigations into the cases of Sharif and more than 30 other people detained at the same time as part of the group did not prove the charges.
The Interior Ministry information centre said on Sunday it had no information on the case.
